title: US Citizenship Interview: What to Expect on the Day
excerpt: What happens at your naturalization interview, and how to feel ready for it.
description: What to expect at your US citizenship (naturalization) interview: the application review, the English test, the civics test and how to prepare.
body:
At your US citizenship interview, a USCIS officer reviews your Form N-400 application with you and gives you the English and civics tests. Knowing what to expect makes the day much less stressful.

## What happens

- The officer places you under oath and asks questions about your application
- You take the English test: reading, writing and speaking
- You take the civics test: the officer asks questions about US government and history, and you answer out loud

## What to bring

Bring your interview notice, your green card, and every document listed in your interview notice. Check the notice carefully, because it lists what applies to you.

## Tips

- Practise answering civics questions out loud, not just reading them
- Know your application well, since the officer may ask about anything in it
- Check answers that change, like your senators and representative, before the day

## After the interview

If you pass and your application is approved, you're invited to an oath ceremony. If you fail part of the test, you usually get one more chance at a second interview.

Check uscis.gov for the latest information. Try a free civics practice test below.
